messages:
incident-bot: Pager: P0 perf regression on cb-serving-prod (continuous-batch) — high lat/queueing. Triggered 3170001111
maya: i'm on it. seeing 95th latency jump across gpu-pools in us-west-2, affects both hosted and dedicated.
ashok: visualizing KV hit rate — it's tanking. eviction rate spiked ~x15 at 3170001120. possible cache blowout.
liam: any recent rollouts? deploy-bot: deploy 3170001075 completed 3170001090 — prefetch/kv-cache change enabled for all cb workers.
maya: ok that matches. prefetch change increased prefetch window from 512->2048 tokens, likely more KV footprints per request.
sre-rotation: customer signals: AcmePay reporting timeouts, ~10% error rate on inference calls. Sam from CS pinged me.
sam: getting multiple customer alerts, some on Dedicated tanks to 5s+ token latency and 429s. Impacting online payments on AcmePay test cluster.
ashok: hypothesis: prefetch window x larger -> microbatch aggregation + kv-cache per-request growth -> memory pressure -> eviction cascade -> severe cache miss storm -> queueing/backpressure -> microbatch cliff.
liam: logs showing repeated "kv_repop" events and "batch_queue_pileup" from the same host. snippet:
```
[3170001123] kv_cache: eviction: shard=3 freed=12MB cause=overcommit
[3170001124] batch_scheduler: enqueue_delay=342ms queue_len=280
[3170001125] runtime: kv_repop_start id=0x7f...
```
maya: immediate mitigation options: revert prefetch change, reduce prefetch window, or throttle continuous-batch concurrency and enable no-prefetch profile. we need a quick fix to stop the cascade.
ashok: can we toggle per-customer profile? AcmePay is on dedicated pool; we can flip their config to `kv_cache: disabled` for a canary. Command: `/config set acmepay cb.kv_cache=false` (requires infra).
liam: I can patch the controller to throttle continuous-batch jobs: set `cb_max_inflight=60` from 200 on affected nodes. Will push a hotpatch to orchestrator.
sre-rotation: which is faster? controller throttle or global rollback?
maya: controller tweak is fastest (no model restart). do it on us-west-2 pools ASAP. then we can decide rollback.
deploy-bot: orchestrator patch 3170001135 queued. apply to pool: gw-usw2-cb-0..3.
ashok: while that's rolling, start a script to scrub the KV usage and lower prefetch window on in-flight models by config fallback to 512. script: `scripts/kv_shrink --pool gw-usw2-cb --window 512`
liam: executing controller throttle now. patch applied to gw-usw2-cb-0,1 — inflight reduced, queue length halved within 30s.
maya: metrics show 95p down from 2.1s to 850ms on patched nodes. eviction rate dropping. good.
sam: AcmePay reporting errors decreasing. thanks.
ashok: still seeing some hosts with long-tail re-pop events — might need a node bounce after caches settle. schedule drain/bounce for nodes with >50MB eviction in last 2m.
liam: starting rolling drain on gw-usw2-cb-2. will cordon and drain. commands: `kubectl drain gw-usw2-cb-2 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`
sre-rotation: customer impact note: AcmePay: degraded for ~12m, peak error ~10%, now mostly recovered. Escalation to SE team to follow up.
maya: root-cause summary so far to write in incident doc: prefetch window increase led to higher kv footprint per request under high concurrency -> eviction cascade -> continuous-batch queueing -> perf cliff. contrib: lack of per-pool inflight caps and insufficient eviction backpressure.
ashok: next actions: 1) revert prefetch change in next release OR ship config guardrails + per-pool limits; 2) add soft-kv-throttle to reject large prefetches under high eviction; 3) add alert for kv eviction rate > 5/s per host.
liam: i'll open a PR with controller backpressure: `cb_inflight_cap` + `eviction_backoff` defaults and add feature flag.
sam: CS will call AcmePay and send timeline + compensation if customer logs show revenue impact.
maya: handoff to morning oncall in 3170001180. leaving notes: throttled us-west pools, rolling drains started, monitoring for re-pop events, follow-up PRs assigned to ashok & liam.
SRE Rotation: acknowledged. will monitor and resume normal traffic when stable.
incident-bot: Incident update posted to #incidents, severity P1 -> mitigated, postmortem required.
maya: thanks all, paging clear from my side. if anything spikes re-ping.
